But vvhen he vvrote the Second to them (vvhere in the 11 Chapter he maketh mention of 14 yeres, not onely after his Conuer{{ls}}ion, as to the Galatians, but al{{ls}}o after his Rapte, vvhich {{ls}}eemeth to haue bene vvhen he vvas at Hieru{{ls}}alem Act. 9. foure yeres after his Conuer{{ls}}ion, ''in a traunce,'' as he calleth it Act. 22, 17) then vvere they readie. Cor. 9: ''For the vvhich I doe glorie of you to the Macedonians: that al{{ls}}o Achaia is ready from the yere pa{{ls}}t.'' hovvbeit it folovveth theire: ''But I haue {{ls}}ent the brethren, that (as I haue {{ls}}aid) you may be ready: le{{ls}}t vvhen the Macedonians come vvith me, and find you vnready, vve be a{{ls}}hamed.'' But vvhen he vvrote to the Romanes, then vvas he novv come to Corinth for the purpo{{ls}}e, and had receiued theire contribution, and vvas readie to goe vvith it vnto Hieru{{ls}}alem. For Macedonia and Achaia haue liked vvel to make {{ls}}ome cōtribution vpō the poore {{ls}}aincts that are in Hieru{{ls}}alem.''{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The argument of the Epi{{ls}}tle to the Romanes.}}

So then, the Epi{{ls}}tle to the Romanes vvas not the fir{{ls}}t that he vvrote. But yet it is*{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=* ''Epih. Hæer. 42. Marcionis. Aug. in Expo{{ls}}. incho. Ep. ad Rom.''}} and alvvaies vvas {{ls}}et fir{{ls}}t, becau{{ls}}e of the primacie of that Church, for vvhich cau{{ls}}e al{{ls}}o he handleth in it, {{ls}}uch matters as perteined not to them alone, but to the vniuer{{ls}}al Church, and {{ls}}pecially to al the Gentiles: to vvit, the very frame (as it vvere) of the Church of Chri{{ls}}t. Augu{{ls}}tine, giuing vs briefly the argument. in english thus: ''As being a legate for our Lord him {{ls}}elf, that is, for the corner {{ls}}tone, he knitteth together in Chri{{ls}}t by the bād of Grace, both peoples, as vvel of the Ievves as of the Gentils.'' Shevving, that neither of them had in their Gentilitie or Iudai{{ls}}me any vvorkes to bragge of, or to chalenge to them {{ls}}elues iu{{ls}}tification or {{ls}}aluation thereby, but rather {{ls}}innes they had to be {{ls}}orie for, and to humble them {{ls}}elues to the faith of Chri{{ls}}t, that {{ls}}o they might haue remi{{ls}}sion of them, and {{ls}}trength to doe meritorius vvorkes aftervvard. In vvhich {{ls}}ort, becau{{ls}}e the Gentils did humble them {{ls}}elues, therefore had they found mercy, though they neuer vvi{{ls}}t of the Lavv of Moy{{ls}}es. But the Ievves, becau{{ls}}e they {{ls}}toode vpon their ovvne vvorkes, vvhich they did by their ovvne {{ls}}trength, vvith the knovvledge of the Lavv (being therefore al{{ls}}o called ''the vvorkes of the Lavv,''){{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The vvorkes of the Lavv.}} & {{ls}}o would not humble them {{ls}}elues to beleeue in Chri{{ls}}t crucified, they mi{{ls}}{{ls}}ed of mercy, and became reprobate, excepting a few ''Reliquiae'' that God of his goodnes had re{{ls}}erued to him {{ls}}elf. Hovvbeit in the end, vvhen the fulnes of the Gentils is come into the Church, then {{ls}}hal the fulnes of the Ievves al{{ls}}o open their eies, acknowledge their errour, and {{ls}}ubmit them {{ls}}elues to Chri{{ls}}t and his Church, in like maner.
